title: arXiv Mathematics — notable papers in the Friday, 6 November 2026 batch
global_caveat: arXiv publishes no official trending chart; this ordering is inferred, not measured popularity. Citation evidence is limited for papers announced only days ago, and no citation-based ordering is used.

sections.title: Resolving Tusnády's Problem
sections.abstract: The author proves a matching lower bound of order (log N)^(d-1/2) for combinatorial discrepancy of anchored boxes in each fixed dimension d≥3, which—combined with existing upper and planar lower bounds—settles the order for axis-parallel boxes in all fixed dimensions d≥2.
sections.claimed_result: Theorem 1.1 gives disc(N,A_d)≥c_d(log N)^(d−1/2) for all sufficiently large N and each fixed d≥3; with cited bounds, Corollary 1.2 gives Θ_d((log N)^(d−1/2)). Author's preprint claim.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Worst-case combinatorial discrepancy for N-point sets against anchored or axis-parallel boxes in Euclidean d-space; d is fixed, and constants and threshold may depend on d.
sections.unique_caveat: The author does not optimize dimension-dependent constants or threshold; the new lower-bound proof treats d≥3 and relies on a prior planar lower bound for d=2.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The main theorem closes the remaining factor-sqrt(log N) gap for every fixed d≥3; the abstract identifies the earlier matching upper bound and planar result. A second same-batch preprint independently claims the sharp order.

sections.title: Tusnády's problem and online two-sample thinning
sections.abstract: The author proves the same sharp discrepancy order in every fixed dimension, a robust lower bound after limited deletions, and minimax bounds for online thinning of two samples, including a sharp one-dimensional terminal rate.
sections.claimed_result: Theorem 1.1 states Δ_d(N)=Θ_d((log N)^(d−1/2)) for fixed d≥2. Theorem 1.2 gives minimax expected prefix discrepancy Θ_(k,ρ)((log n)^(k+1/2)) for fixed k≥1 and 0<ρ<2; for k=1, terminal discrepancy is Θ_ρ((log log n)^(3/2)). Author's preprint claims.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Geometry result for worst-case finite point sets and axis-parallel boxes. Thinning uses two independent size-n samples from an unknown common Borel law; keep/discard decisions are online and irrevocable with expected deletion budget ρn.
sections.unique_caveat: For k≥2, terminal discrepancy bounds remain separated by a factor of log n; the sharp prefix order does not close this gap.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Same-batch independent proof of the sharp Tusnády order plus additional quantitative online-thinning results; cross-lists combinatorics, algorithms, and probability.

sections.title: An extremal unimodular lattice of rank 37
sections.abstract: The author constructs a rank-37 extremal unimodular lattice of minimum four, resolving the last undetermined optimal minimum through rank 48, and derives a corresponding Type I self-dual Z/4Z code.
sections.claimed_result: The main theorem constructs an integral unimodular lattice of rank 37 and minimum four, automorphism group AGL(1,13)×C6, with a 4-frame yielding a Type I self-dual Z/4Z code of length 37 and minimum Euclidean weight 16.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Positive-definite integral unimodular lattices; minimum is the smallest squared norm of a nonzero lattice vector. The code conclusion uses a 4-frame.
sections.unique_caveat: The coding result depends on exhibiting a 4-frame; the paper reports a computer search and specifies representatives in an appendix. The result addresses rank 37, not higher ranks.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The introduction identifies rank 37 as the sole unresolved optimal-minimum case through rank 48; the construction also settles the matching length-37 code case and links lattice theory to coding theory.

sections.title: On do Carmo's Question: The Properly Embedded Case
sections.abstract: The author claims every complete, noncompact, two-sided, properly embedded CMC hypersurface of finite Morse index in Euclidean space is minimal in every dimension, without curvature or volume-growth bounds.
sections.claimed_result: Theorem 1 states that a smooth, connected, complete, noncompact, two-sided, properly embedded CMC hypersurface without boundary and finite Morse index in R^(n+1) has zero mean curvature for every n≥2.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Complete, noncompact, two-sided, properly embedded, boundaryless, finite-index hypersurface in Euclidean space; proof uses an inscribed-radius weight and stability outside a compact set.
sections.unique_caveat: Proper embeddedness is essential to the presented argument; the theorem does not cover arbitrary immersed hypersurfaces in every dimension.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The theorem removes dimension restrictions and curvature/volume-growth bounds for the properly embedded finite-index case; the introduction contrasts it with earlier bounded-curvature or limited-dimension results.

sections.title: Pointless K3 surfaces over finite fields
sections.abstract: The authors prove a K3 surface without a rational point over F_q exists exactly for prime powers q≤11, using lattice bounds, the Artin–Tate formula, and Niemeier-lattice embeddings.
sections.claimed_result: The authors claim a K3 surface without an F_q-point exists if and only if q≤11; they also state this improves a bound used in certain threefold rational-point results.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Smooth K3 surfaces over finite fields with q a prime power; conclusion concerns existence of at least one rational point over the field of definition.
sections.unique_caveat: The approach uses numerical computations and lattice-embedding analysis; an independent preprint by Brandhorst and Takada, arXiv:2611.06366, reports the same classification by a different method.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Sharp existence/nonexistence cutoff in arithmetic geometry, linking finite-field point counts to lattice packing and Niemeier embeddings; paper notes an independent proof.

sections.title: Weak uniqueness for the stochastic heat equation with nondegenerate diffusion: the full Hölder regime
sections.abstract: The author claims weak well-posedness for a one-dimensional torus stochastic heat equation with uniformly nondegenerate diffusion coefficient Hölder continuous at any positive exponent, extending an earlier result above 2/3.
sections.claimed_result: The author claims weak well-posedness for the scalar stochastic heat equation on the one-dimensional torus with uniformly nondegenerate, positively Hölder diffusion, and extends the argument to measurable drifts of linear growth by localized Girsanov change of measure.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Scalar equation on the one-dimensional torus; diffusion uniformly nondegenerate and Hölder continuous with exponent α>0. Drift extension is to measurable drifts of linear growth.
sections.unique_caveat: The claim is weak well-posedness, not pathwise uniqueness; the 121-page proof and linked Lean formalization were not independently audited here.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract claims closure of the full positive-Hölder range left open by the author's earlier preprint and links a Lean formalization; it is a substantial stochastic-PDE problem.

sections.title: Global well-posedness for the energy-critical focusing NLS on $\mathbb T^3$
sections.abstract: The authors claim global well-posedness for the focusing quintic NLS on the standard three-torus for data below mass-corrected energy and Sobolev thresholds set by the Euclidean ground state.
sections.claimed_result: The authors claim global well-posedness and uniform finite-interval bounds under their subthreshold conditions for the energy-critical focusing NLS on T^3.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Standard flat three-torus; focusing quintic energy-critical NLS; initial data satisfy mass-corrected energy and Sobolev-norm thresholds tied to the Euclidean ground state.
sections.unique_caveat: The theorem is subthreshold and does not cover data at or above the stated ground-state conditions.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Presented as a subthreshold focusing counterpart to a known defocusing theorem; combines periodic profile analysis with a recent Euclidean scattering theorem.

sections.title: Uniqueness of Extremizers and Convergence of the Euler-Lagrange Iteration for the Critical Hardy-Littlewood-Sobolev Inequality
sections.abstract: For n≥3, 2≤α<n, and p^−1+r^−1=1+α/n, the author claims uniqueness of normalized nonnegative extremizers up to translations and dilations, radial nondegeneracy, and convergence of an alternating iteration from nonnegative radially nonincreasing data.
sections.claimed_result: The author claims positive finite-energy Euler–Lagrange solutions lie in a single translation/dilation orbit, and normalized alternating iteration converges strongly to an extremizing pair from every nonnegative radially nonincreasing initial datum.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: n≥3, 2≤α<n, 1<p,r<∞, p^−1+r^−1=1+α/n; iteration additionally assumes nonnegative, radially nonincreasing initial data.
sections.unique_caveat: The convergence guarantee is for radial nonincreasing initial data; it does not establish convergence from arbitrary nonnegative data.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Combines uniqueness for a critical integral inequality with a convergence result for its Euler–Lagrange iteration; cross-listed between PDE and classical analysis.

sections.title: A diameter-one set in $\mathbb{R}^5$ that cannot be covered by six diameter-one balls
sections.abstract: The authors construct a compact diameter-one set in R^5 that cannot be covered by six diameter-one balls, with a finite-set version resisting six balls of radius 0.50001.
sections.claimed_result: The authors claim a compact set of diameter 1 in R^5 not coverable by six Euclidean balls of diameter 1; its convex hull also has this property, and a finite subset remains uncovered by six closed balls of radius 0.50001.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Euclidean metric in dimension five; covering by six balls, with diameter one in the compact-set statement and the specified larger radius in the finite-set statement.
sections.unique_caveat: The construction and conclusion are dimension- and covering-number-specific; the abstract does not assert a general formula for other dimensions or numbers of balls.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Concrete counterexample to a covering assertion, including a finite witness with a stated radius margin; proof connects a matrix-space construction to spherical coverings and Euler's formula.

sections.title: Trending Research Themes
text: Two independent same-batch claims resolve the fixed-dimensional Tusnády order. Wengiel proves the d≥3 lower bound and combines it with prior results; Lei proves the sharp order for d≥2 and uses robust discrepancy for online two-sample thinning. Their proofs are distinct, though both connect discrepancy with Gaussian methods.

Kubischta's rank-37 construction yields a self-dual code; Auel, Engel, Kedlaya, and Shaikh use definite lattices and Niemeier embeddings to constrain K3 zeta functions. These are distinct results linked by lattice structure.

Niu's CMC theorem, Chen–Wang's focusing NLS result, Han's weak uniqueness theorem, and Lu's HLS results span geometric analysis, dispersive PDE, stochastic PDE, and critical inequalities. They are isolated contributions rather than evidence of a shared method or field-wide shift.

sections.title: Open Problems and Research Directions
text: Author-stated limitation: Wengiel's constants and thresholds depend on fixed dimension and are not optimized; proposed direction is to seek explicit dimension dependence or sharper finite-N thresholds.
Author-stated gap: Lei's terminal minimax upper and lower bounds for k≥2 differ by a factor of log n; closing the gap is an explicit next problem.
Scope-based direction: Niu's theorem requires proper embeddedness; investigate geometric hypotheses that might replace properness in the all-dimensional finite-index setting.
Scope-based direction: Lu proves HLS iteration convergence from nonnegative radially nonincreasing data; test whether weaker assumptions suffice for a wider initial-data class.
Scope-based direction: Chen and Wang's focusing NLS theorem is below ground-state thresholds; the equality case merits separate analysis, without assuming the paper labels it open.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.text: The clearest headline is the independent pair of preprints claiming the sharp fixed-dimensional order in Tusnády's problem, with Lei adding an online-thinning application and a precisely stated remaining terminal gap. Other selected papers include a rank-37 lattice construction and sharp claims in geometry and analysis; all remain preprints, and this is result-driven notability rather than measured popularity.
